### [OnConflict](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html)

OnConflict 
What an insert does when the row would break a primary key or a unique constraint or index. 
Set on each row before <code>SubmitUpdates</code>; rows of one submit may differ. Databases without an upsert
 (SQL Server, Oracle, Firebird, ODBC, MS Access) ignore <code>Update</code> and <code>DoNothing</code> and refuse
 <code>DoNothingOn</code> and <code>UpdateOn</code>. A row inserted without its key reads the key the database gave it; after a
 conflict it reads the existing row's key when that row was updated, and none when it was left as it was. 
OnConflict.IsUpdateOn 
IsUpdateOn 
OnConflict.IsDoNothingOn 
IsDoNothingOn 
OnConflict.IsDoNothing 
IsDoNothing 
OnConflict.IsUpdate 
IsUpdate 
OnConflict.IsThrow 
IsThrow 
OnConflict.Throw 
Throw 
OnConflict.Update 
Update 
OnConflict.DoNothing 
DoNothing 
OnConflict.DoNothingOn 
DoNothingOn 
OnConflict.UpdateOn 
UpdateOn

### [OnConflict.IsUpdateOn](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#IsUpdateOn)

OnConflict.IsUpdateOn 
IsUpdateOn

### [OnConflict.IsDoNothingOn](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#IsDoNothingOn)

OnConflict.IsDoNothingOn 
IsDoNothingOn

### [OnConflict.IsDoNothing](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#IsDoNothing)

OnConflict.IsDoNothing 
IsDoNothing

### [OnConflict.IsUpdate](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#IsUpdate)

OnConflict.IsUpdate 
IsUpdate

### [OnConflict.IsThrow](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#IsThrow)

OnConflict.IsThrow 
IsThrow

### [OnConflict.Throw](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#Throw)

OnConflict.Throw 
Throw 
The insert fails with the database's error (the default).

### [OnConflict.Update](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#Update)

OnConflict.Update 
Update 
The existing row gets every column the new row sets. 
PostgreSQL: <code>ON CONFLICT (primary key) DO UPDATE</code>; DuckDB the same; MySQL:
 <code>ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE</code>; SQLite: <code>INSERT OR REPLACE</code>, which deletes the existing row and inserts the new
 one, so columns not set get their defaults and delete triggers and cascades run.

### [OnConflict.DoNothing](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#DoNothing)

OnConflict.DoNothing 
DoNothing 
The existing row stays as it is, whichever unique constraint the new row breaks. 
PostgreSQL and DuckDB: <code>ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING</code>; MySQL: <code>ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE</code> of nothing;
 SQLite: <code>INSERT OR IGNORE</code>.

### [OnConflict.DoNothingOn](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#DoNothingOn)

OnConflict.DoNothingOn 
DoNothingOn 
The existing row stays as it is when the new row breaks the unique constraint or index on exactly these
 columns: <code>ON CONFLICT (columns) DO NOTHING</code>. 
PostgreSQL, SQLite 3.24+ and DuckDB; MySQL refuses it.

### [OnConflict.UpdateOn](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-onconflict.html#UpdateOn)

OnConflict.UpdateOn 
UpdateOn 
The existing row changes when the new row breaks the unique constraint or index on exactly
 <code>onColumns</code>: <code>ON CONFLICT (onColumns) DO UPDATE SET a = EXCLUDED.a, b = @value</code>. 
PostgreSQL, SQLite 3.24+ and DuckDB; MySQL refuses it.

### [SqlEntity.CloneTo](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-common-sqlentity.html#CloneTo)

SqlEntity.CloneTo 
CloneTo 
 Attach/copy entity to a different data-context.
 Second parameter: SQL UPDATE or INSERT clause?  
 UPDATE: Updates the exising database entity with the values that this entity contains.
 INSERT: Makes a copy of entity (database row), which is a new row with the same columns and values (except Id)

### [QueryInspection](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-runtime-queryinspection.html)

QueryInspection 
 Query debugging and inspection utilities 
QueryInspection.IQueryableExtensions 
IQueryableExtensions 
QueryInspection.toQueryString 
toQueryString

### [QueryInspection.toQueryString](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-runtime-queryinspection.html#toQueryString)

QueryInspection.toQueryString 
toQueryString 
 Generates the SQL query string and parameters without executing the query.
 Note: This function creates a database connection to access schema metadata for SQL generation,
 but does not execute any queries against the database.
 This is useful for debugging, logging, or when you need to execute the query through ADO.NET directly.
 Returns a tuple of (SQL query string, array of parameter name-value pairs).

### [IQueryableExtensions](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-runtime-queryinspection-iqueryableextensions.html)

IQueryableExtensions 
 Extension methods for IQueryable to provide EF Core-like query inspection capabilities 
IQueryableExtensions.ToQueryString 
ToQueryString

### [IQueryableExtensions.ToQueryString](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-runtime-queryinspection-iqueryableextensions.html#ToQueryString)

IQueryableExtensions.ToQueryString 
ToQueryString 
 Generates the SQL query string and parameters without executing the query.
 Note: This method creates a database connection to access schema metadata for SQL generation,
 but does not execute any queries against the database.
 This is useful for debugging, logging, or when you need to execute the query through ADO.NET directly.
 Returns a tuple of (SQL query string, array of parameter name-value pairs).

### [TransactionUtils](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-transactionutils.html)

TransactionUtils 
 Utility functions for converting between different transaction isolation level representations. 
TransactionUtils.toSystemDataIsolationLevel 
toSystemDataIsolationLevel 
TransactionUtils.ensureTransaction 
ensureTransaction

### [TransactionUtils.toSystemDataIsolationLevel](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-transactionutils.html#toSystemDataIsolationLevel)

TransactionUtils.toSystemDataIsolationLevel 
toSystemDataIsolationLevel 
 Converts SQL provider isolation level to System.Data.IsolationLevel.
 Use this when you need to work directly with ADO.NET connection transactions.
 param isolationLevel: The SQL provider isolation level
 returns: The corresponding System.Data.IsolationLevel

### [TransactionUtils.ensureTransaction](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-transactionutils.html#ensureTransaction)

TransactionUtils.ensureTransaction 
ensureTransaction 
 Creates the TransactionScope that wraps a SubmitUpdates write batch. Called ONLY from the
 providers' ProcessUpdates/ProcessUpdatesAsync - reads are never wrapped. Uses
 TransactionScopeOption.Required: if the caller already opened an ambient transaction this
 enlists in it (and the caller's isolation level applies, not the one passed here); otherwise
 it starts a fresh standalone transaction using transactionOptions. Pass
 IsolationLevel.DontCreateTransaction to skip creating a scope entirely.

### [IsolationLevel](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html)

IsolationLevel 
 Transaction isolation level for database operations.
 Corresponds to the System.Transactions.IsolationLevel but provides SQL provider specific functionality.
 Only applied when SubmitUpdates creates its own (standalone) write transaction; if you wrap your
 own ambient System.Transactions scope, that scope's isolation level is used instead. 
IsolationLevel.Serializable 
Serializable 
IsolationLevel.RepeatableRead 
RepeatableRead 
IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted 
ReadCommitted 
IsolationLevel.ReadUncommitted 
ReadUncommitted 
IsolationLevel.Snapshot 
Snapshot 
IsolationLevel.Chaos 
Chaos 
IsolationLevel.Unspecified 
Unspecified 
IsolationLevel.DontCreateTransaction 
DontCreateTransaction

### [IsolationLevel.Serializable](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#Serializable)

IsolationLevel.Serializable 
Serializable 
 Highest isolation level - transactions are completely isolated from each other

### [IsolationLevel.RepeatableRead](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#RepeatableRead)

IsolationLevel.RepeatableRead 
RepeatableRead 
 Prevents dirty reads and non-repeatable reads, but phantom reads can occur

### [IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#ReadCommitted)

IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted 
ReadCommitted 
 Prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads and phantom reads.
 (This describes the default isolation of most DB *engines* - it is NOT SQLProvider's default;
 TransactionOptions.Default is Serializable, inherited from System.Transactions.)

### [IsolationLevel.ReadUncommitted](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#ReadUncommitted)

IsolationLevel.ReadUncommitted 
ReadUncommitted 
 Allows dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads (fastest but least safe)

### [IsolationLevel.Snapshot](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#Snapshot)

IsolationLevel.Snapshot 
Snapshot 
 SQL Server specific - provides statement-level read consistency using versioning

### [IsolationLevel.Chaos](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#Chaos)

IsolationLevel.Chaos 
Chaos 
 Allows any level of isolation, including overlapping changes (SQL Server specific)

### [IsolationLevel.Unspecified](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#Unspecified)

IsolationLevel.Unspecified 
Unspecified 
 Use the default isolation level of the database

### [IsolationLevel.DontCreateTransaction](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-isolationlevel.html#DontCreateTransaction)

IsolationLevel.DontCreateTransaction 
DontCreateTransaction 
 Special value to indicate that no transaction should be created

### [TransactionOptions](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-transactionoptions.html)

TransactionOptions 
 Configuration options for database transactions.
 Corresponds to the System.Transactions.TransactionOptions.

Default 
TransactionOptions.Timeout 
Timeout 
TransactionOptions.IsolationLevel 
IsolationLevel

### [TransactionOptions.Default](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/fsharp-data-sql-transactions-transactionoptions.html#Default)

TransactionOptions.Default 
Default 
 Inherits System.Transactions' defaults: Timeout = 1 minute and IsolationLevel = Serializable.
 The Serializable level only applies to a standalone SubmitUpdates write batch (no ambient
 transaction); wrap your read-then-write work in your own scope to control isolation. See the
 note on the IsolationLevel type above.

TransactionOptions.Timeout 
Timeout 
 Maximum time the transaction can remain active before timing out

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

### [Methods.``not false is true``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``not false is true``)

Methods.``not false is true`` 
``not false is true`` 
 not(false) -> true 
 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

### [Methods.``evaluate basic constant math``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``evaluate basic constant math``)

``evaluate basic constant math`` 
 A fold that overflows here (decimal arithmetic is always checked) is left in
 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

### [Methods.``not false is true``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``not false is true``)

Methods.``not false is true`` 
``not false is true`` 
 not(false) -> true 
 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

balancetree

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

### [Methods.``evaluate basic constant math``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``evaluate basic constant math``)

Methods.``evaluate basic constant math`` 
``evaluate basic constant math`` 
 A fold that overflows here (decimal arithmetic is always checked) is left in
 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-0.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-2.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-2.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-2.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-2.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-3.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-3.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-4.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

Methods.``remove mutually exclusive condition`` 
``remove mutually exclusive condition``

``evaluate constants``

### [Methods.``evaluate basic constant math``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-4.html#``evaluate basic constant math``)

Methods.``evaluate basic constant math`` 
``evaluate basic constant math`` 
 A fold that overflows here (decimal arithmetic is always checked) is left in
 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-4.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-4.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-4.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-5.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-5.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-5.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

Methods.``not false is true`` 
``not false is true`` 
 not(false) -> true 
 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-7.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-7.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-7.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-7.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-7.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-7.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-9.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

``evaluate basic constant math``

 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-9.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-9.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-9.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-10.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-10.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-10.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

### [Methods.``not false is true``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-10.html#``not false is true``)

Methods.``not false is true`` 
``not false is true`` 
 not(false) -> true 
 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-12.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-12.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-12.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

``not false is true``

 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-12.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-12.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-14.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-14.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-14.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-14.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.balancetree](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-16.html#balancetree)

Methods.balancetree 
balancetree 
 Balance tree that is too much weighted to other side.
 The real advantage is not-so-nested-stack

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-16.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

### [Methods.``evaluate basic constant math``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-16.html#``evaluate basic constant math``)

``evaluate basic constant math``

 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-16.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-16.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-16.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-17.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-17.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-17.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

Methods.``not false is true`` 
``not false is true`` 
 not(false) -> true 
 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

### [Methods.``replace constant comparison``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``replace constant comparison``)

Methods.``replace constant comparison`` 
``replace constant comparison`` 
<pre> The purpose of this is to optimize away already known constant=constant style expressions.
   7 > 8      -->   False
 "G" = "G"    -->   True
 Only a comparison by value that returns bool: a built-in operator, and not the
 reference comparison of two objects (no Method on reference-typed operands).</pre>

### [Methods.``remove AnonymousType``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``remove AnonymousType``)

Methods.``remove AnonymousType`` 
``remove AnonymousType`` 
 Purpose of this is to replace non-used anonymous types:
 new AnonymousObject(Item1 = x, Item2 = "").Item1    -->   x
 The member's constructor argument is found through NewExpression.Members (the
 member at index i is initialised from argument i), for a tuple without Members
 through its ItemN, and for an anonymous type without Members by the name of
 the member the argument reads.

### [Methods.``cut not used condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``cut not used condition``)

Methods.``cut not used condition`` 
``cut not used condition`` 
 if false then x else y -> y 
 (a branch of the conditional's own type only: a typed conditional keeps its type)

### [Methods.``not false is true``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``not false is true``)

Methods.``not false is true`` 
``not false is true`` 
 not(false) -> true 
 (a plain bool constant only: Not on a Nullable<bool> constant stays Nullable<bool>)

### [Methods.``remove duplicate condition``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``remove duplicate condition``)

Methods.``remove duplicate condition`` 
``remove duplicate condition`` 
 The later of two equal comparisons in one And'/Or' chain goes. Behind a
 short-circuit link (AndAlso, OrElse, a conditional) the right side runs only
 once the left side is true (false for Or'), so a comparison the left chain
 already holds is true (false) there. The earlier one stays, so nothing that
 was guarded by it runs ahead of it. Behind And/Or the right side runs
 regardless, and taking a comparison out of it would unguard what followed
 it there, so only a right side that is the comparison itself goes.

 the tree for the run time to throw.

### [Methods.``simplify string operations``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``simplify string operations``)

Methods.``simplify string operations`` 
``simplify string operations`` 
 String concatenation with empty string optimization
 "" + x -> x, x + "" -> x
 Only when x cannot be null: null + "" is "" (String.Concat), while x alone
 stays null, so `(x + "").Length` would go from 0 to a NullReferenceException.

### [Methods.``simplify conditionals``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``simplify conditionals``)

Methods.``simplify conditionals`` 
``simplify conditionals`` 
 Simplify conditional expressions 
 x ? true : false -> x, x ? false : true -> !x, x ? y : y -> y

### [Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities``](https://fsprojects.github.io/SQLProvider/reference/expressionoptimizer-methods-19.html#``simplify arithmetic identities``)

Methods.``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
``simplify arithmetic identities`` 
 Additional arithmetic identity optimizations
 x - 0 -> x, x - x -> 0, x % 1 -> 0
